details.description: Aura is Deepgram's first-generation text-to-speech model, offering a catalog of 12 English voices for real-time speech synthesis through Deepgram's Speak API. Each voice is documented with a set of characteristics (for example clear, warm or confident) and a recommended use case such as advertising, IVR or customer service. Deepgram's Speak API still defaults to an Aura voice (aura-asteria-en) when no model is specified, even after the release of the newer, multilingual Aura-2 family.
advantages: Is the Deepgram Speak API's default voice model (aura-asteria-en) when no model is specified, per Deepgram's Text-to-Speech guide.
Offers 12 distinct English voices, each documented with characteristics and a recommended use case, per Deepgram's TTS Models documentation.
Streams audio back as it is generated so playback can begin as soon as the first byte arrives, per Deepgram's Text-to-Speech guide.
disadvantages: English only, while Deepgram's newer Aura-2 model adds voices in additional languages including Spanish, German, French, Dutch, Italian and Japanese, per Deepgram's TTS Models documentation.
use_cases: Interactive voice response (IVR) prompts, e.g. the luna and zeus voices, per Deepgram's TTS Models documentation.
Customer service voice agents, e.g. the stella, arcas, perseus and helios voices, per Deepgram's TTS Models documentation.
Advertising voiceovers, e.g. the asteria voice, per Deepgram's TTS Models documentation.
Storytelling and narration, e.g. the athena, angus and orpheus voices, per Deepgram's TTS Models documentation.
Informative announcements, e.g. the hera and orion voices, per Deepgram's TTS Models documentation.

notes: Deepgram's TTS Models and Text-to-Speech docs never call Aura (v1) legacy, deprecated or superseded; aura-asteria-en remains the documented API default even after Aura-2 shipped, so no legacy claim is made here. No word-error-rate or other accuracy figure was found for Aura, so evaluations is left empty. Catalog carries no deprecation_date.
